Is your technology foundation[ready for agentic commerce](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/agentic-commerce-readiness-assessment) ?


You have faced this question before. As customer expectations changed, you had to decide whether your stack could support hyper-personalized search, frictionless checkout, social commerce, new payment methods, and stronger loyalty without rebuilding everything.


Patching a monolithic stack may have worked for previous shifts. It will not be enough when AI agents move from discovery to transaction and payment at machine speed, exposing every crack in your systems and data behind the journey. Outdated price or stock data in real-time feeds causes[26% of agent abandonments](https://www.gspann.com/insights/blog/agentic-commerce-experience-vs-customer-experience) , while discrepancies between catalog and checkout pricing account for[18% of failed transactions](https://rapidcents.com/en-ca/resources/how-abandoned-carts-and-failed-transactions-are-killing-sales-in-2025) .


Agent cart abandonment stands at 78.6%, above the roughly 70% benchmark for human shoppers.


Source:[Agent Cart Abandonment Statistics 2026, Presenc AI](https://presenc.ai/research/agent-cart-abandonment-statistics-2026)


## What leading retailers are doing differently?


They have already built open, connected, and composable commerce foundations around[MACH principles](https://www.griddynamics.com/glossary/mach-architecture) : microservices-based, API-first, cloud-native, and headless. These foundations were designed to adapt to new customer expectations without rebuilding the stack each time. Now, they give businesses the reliable data, accessible business capabilities, and independent scale that agents need to act.


That flexibility is creating a measurable advantage for[AI in composable commerce](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/ai-composable-commerce-ebook) . The MACH Alliance Enterprise Technology Report found that[78% of companies with mature composable technology achieve clear AI ROI](https://machalliance.org/insights-hub/mach-alliance-research-6x-more-organizations-achieve-ai-roi-with-a-composable-foundation) , compared with 13% of companies without composable foundations.

## Four ways a composable architecture enables agent-ready commerce design


Skip to the building block that will move your next agentic commerce use case forward.


1.[Modular business capabilities and API access](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/agentic-commerce-architecture#h-1-give-agents-direct-api-access-to-commerce-capabilities) let agents orchestrate end-to-end commerce workflows.


2.[Unified, reliable data](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/agentic-commerce-architecture#h-2-maintain-a-single-source-of-truth-for-reliable-commerce-data) gives agents a real-time source of truth for every commerce decision.


3.[Support all emerging protocols](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/agentic-commerce-architecture#h-3-prepare-for-protocol-agnostic-connectivity) with an open architecture that keeps your commerce capabilities flexible and reusable.


4.[Cloud elasticity scales](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/agentic-commerce-architecture#h-4-scale-for-human-and-ai-driven-demand) search, inventory, payment, and fulfillment as demand from human shoppers and AI agents grows.


## 1. Give agents direct API access to commerce capabilities


An[agentic commerce journey](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/custom-google-shopping-agent-demo) is a series of machine-to-machine API queries and actions. To discover, compare, recommend, and purchase a product, an agent needs structured, reliable access to product attributes, current pricing and promotions, real-time inventory across locations, customer eligibility, fulfillment options, payment status, and order updates.


*The real-time data access agents need at every stage*


But data only creates value when agents can securely retrieve it and act on it across the journey. That is difficult in tightly coupled monolithic systems built around human interfaces. AI agents do not render web pages, execute JavaScript, or click through screens. When clean APIs are unavailable, they must interpret pages or rely on brittle point-to-point integrations. This creates stale information, high latency, unreliable recommendations, and broken transaction flows.


[Composable commerce](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/digital-enterprises-composable-commerce-starter-kit) removes those barriers by exposing catalog, pricing, inventory, order management, payment, and fulfillment as independently callable packaged business capabilities. Agents can retrieve the right data and trigger the right action through governed APIs, without navigating the customer frontend or disrupting unrelated services.


This is what makes agents another headless channel alongside your website, mobile app, marketplace, or customer support tool. The same approved APIs and business rules serve every channel, keeping prices, availability, and order logic consistent while reducing duplicated integrations and technical debt.

## 2. Maintain a single source of truth for reliable commerce data


Even if an agent successfully queries the product catalog, checks a price or payment status, verifies inventory, creates a cart, or triggers fulfillment, the journey can still fail when data is incomplete, outdated, or inconsistent across systems. Recommendations become unreliable. Products that appear available may not be fulfillable. Promotions fail at checkout. Personalization loses relevance. Customers and agents lose trust.


A single source of truth does not require one platform to own everything. It requires clear data ownership and a shared, governed view across PIM, ERP, CRM, pricing, inventory, checkout, payment, order management, fulfillment, and loyalty systems.


- **PIM** owns product attributes, content, and classifications
- **Pricing** owns current prices, promotions, and contract terms
- **Inventory** owns available-to-promise stock by location
- **Order management** owns order status and fulfillment decisions
- **CRM and loyalty** own customer preferences, eligibility, and rewards


[Event-driven integration](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/kafka-composable-commerce-starter-kit) keeps these domains synchronized as conditions change. When stock changes, a price updates, a promotion ends, an order is confirmed, or loyalty points are applied, relevant systems, channels, and agents receive the update without waiting for a batch refresh or manual reconciliation.

### Rich product data behind agent-ready catalogs


Your product catalog determines whether agents can find, understand, compare, and recommend your products, and whether[your brand appears in AI-powered discovery experiences](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/ai-brand-visibility) . Human shoppers can interpret product descriptions, but agents also need structured, machine-readable attributes to make reliable decisions.


*How a modern PIM exposes agent-friendly granular product attributes*


That level of detail requires a PIM to operate as a dedicated, composable capability, not a feature locked inside a monolithic commerce suite. An[AI-driven attribute enrichment](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/product-attribute-enrichment-demo) solution lets teams define, enrich, validate, govern, and expose granular attributes, product relationships, classifications, and channel-specific content through APIs. It can evolve as products, markets, channels, and agent requirements change without forcing changes to the storefront or core transaction platform.

## 3. Prepare for protocol-agnostic connectivity


Reliable, event-driven data gives agents accurate information. Governed APIs give them approved ways to act on that information. To orchestrate end-to-end commerce workflows, agents also need consistent ways to access tools, exchange context, and coordinate with other agents across enterprise systems.


No single protocol covers every need. Emerging standards address different parts of the journey, from agent-to-system access and multi-agent coordination to product discovery, checkout, and payment authorization. The[MACH Alliance Agent Ecosystem](https://machalliance.org/agent-ecosystem) brings technology providers, cloud platforms, AI labs, standards bodies, and open-source initiatives together to develop interoperable reference architectures and enterprise operating patterns around this reality.


Emerging agentic AI protocols include:


**Protocol** **Usage**


**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** Gives an AI application controlled access to enterprise tools, data, and resources.


**Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)** Lets autonomous agents discover one another, delegate work, and exchange results across systems.


**Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)** Defines how an agent and merchant coordinate the shopping flow from product discovery through checkout.


**Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)** Standardizes commerce interactions across agents, merchants, consumer surfaces, and payment providers.


**Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)** Governs delegated payment authorization, using verifiable mandates and policy controls to approve transactions.


For retailers, the priority is not to choose one protocol. It is to avoid tying core commerce capabilities to any one protocol. A composable architecture keeps catalog, pricing, inventory, checkout, payment, and fulfillment independent and API-first. Each capability can then support multiple agent ecosystems through the same business rules, data, security controls, and audit trail.


This matters because custom protocol integrations do not scale. Every new standard can add engineering effort, maintenance, and risk. Reusable APIs and modular capabilities reduce that work, letting you support new agentic use cases across AI-driven and owned channels without repeatedly rebuilding your commerce foundation.


## 4. Scale for human and AI-driven demand


Protocol-agnostic connectivity lets you[introduce new agent experiences](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/ai-agent-retail-sales-case-study) without rebuilding your commerce foundation. That foundation must also handle the demand those experiences create.


AI agents can compare variants, check availability, validate promotions, evaluate delivery options, and execute transactions in milliseconds. At the same time, human shoppers are browsing products, checking store inventory, engaging with loyalty offers, and placing orders. These demand patterns converge on the same commerce foundation. Systems built for predictable, human-paced traffic can struggle under this hybrid load. A surge in catalog search should not slow checkout. A burst of inventory checks should not disrupt pricing. A promotion should not overwhelm fulfillment or loyalty services.


Composable architecture lets you scale the services under pressure instead of scaling the entire platform. Cloud-native elasticity absorbs spikes from campaigns, viral moments, seasonal demand, and growing agent traffic. Event-driven pipelines keep stock, order, payment, and loyalty updates moving as activity increases.


Focus independent scaling on the capabilities that shape conversion and trust:


- [Search and product discovery](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/vertex-ai-search-for-retail-starter-kit) during high-volume browsing
- [Merchandising control](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/merchandising-experience-platform) and flexibility
- [Pricing and inventory](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/inventory-allocation-optimization-starter-kit) validation at checkout
- [Payment and order creation](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/agentic-payments) during transaction peaks
- [Fulfillment and returns](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/order-management-systems) as stores become delivery hubs
- [Loyalty accrual](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/customer-loyalty-platform) , personalized offers, and customer-status updates
- [24/7 AI customer support](https://www.griddynamics.com/solutions/customer-support-ai) across product, order, and inventory inquiries


Scalability is often considered a backend concern. But it impacts everything on the frontline. It determines whether store associates see the right inventory, whether customers receive accurate delivery promises, and whether agents can complete purchases without latency or failure.


Make every[critical journey observable](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/ai-agent-observability-case-study) . Track response times, data freshness, retry rates, validation failures, and transaction outcomes by service and channel. These signals help teams find bottlenecks before they turn into abandoned carts, failed orders, or lost trust.


## Next steps: Assess your agent-readiness


You can wait for AI agents to expose the cracks in your monolithic commerce architecture, or build an open, composable, and connected foundation now. The latter keeps you in control as AI capabilities, protocols, and customer expectations evolve.


- Map the APIs, business capabilities, and data dependencies behind your highest-value journeys.
- Identify where product, pricing, inventory, payment, and fulfillment data becomes delayed, incomplete, or inconsistent.
- Prioritize the foundations agents need to act reliably: governed API access, structured product catalogs, real-time inventory data, and independently scalable services.
- Pilot agent-led journeys alongside existing channels, starting with high-impact use cases such as product discovery or customer support.


The goal is to build a commerce foundation that lets you adopt new capabilities with confidence while keeping experiences accurate, reliable, and scalable for both human shoppers and AI agents.
